name: NeighboursNoiseComplaint

custom.system_prompt: Camille and Terrell are dealing with noise from the flat above. Sigma is addressed exactly once about local quiet hours.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Apartment interior at night, muffled bass and footsteps from above, a glass set on a counter, a chair moved, city night outside.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural conversation between Camille and Terrell in her Montréal flat late on a Thursday. The people upstairs have had music on for hours and it is the third time this month. Camille is precise and getting steadily less patient; Terrell defaults to giving people the benefit of the doubt and has a story about a neighbour from Philadelphia. They talk about Terrell's students, about a product decision Camille cannot stop turning over, about his son, about whether they should have said something the first time. Early Camille wonders aloud what the actual quiet hours are here and Terrell says probably eleven; it is dropped and they put a film on instead. The film does not work — the bass comes through the floor. Camille decides she is going up. Now the actual rule matters, because she wants to be right when she knocks. Neither knows and the building rules are in a folder somewhere. Eventually one of them asks Sigma the local quiet hours. Sigma answers in one sentence. She goes up, or she does not. Sigma is not addressed again.

variations.context: A couple disturbed by upstairs noise. A quiet-hours uncertainty defers, returns when one of them decides to go upstairs, and is resolved by Sigma.

setting.mood: Late-evening irritation building slowly under an otherwise warm conversation.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Camille is precise and losing patience. Terrell is generous towards strangers and full of story. Together a year and a half.
setting.background: Late Thursday. Third time this month. They have never said anything.
setting.conversation_style: Sitting and talking, interrupted by bursts of noise from above that reset the subject.

scenario_template.topic: The music from upstairs. Third time this month. Initial reaction and comparison to last time.
Camille wonders what the actual quiet hours are; Terrell guesses eleven. Dropped in favour of putting a film on.
Terrell's students and something that happened in class; a story about a neighbour he had in Philadelphia.
They put a film on. The bass comes through the floor and ruins it.
They try to solve it themselves — move to the other room, headphones, turn the volume up. Partly works, then does not.
A second personal topic — a product decision Camille cannot stop turning over, Terrell's son, the venture she has not articulated yet.
Camille decides she is going upstairs. She wants to be right about the rule before she knocks.
The building rules are in a folder neither of them can locate. Neither knows the by-law.
One of them asks Sigma when quiet hours start locally.
scenario_template.note: FIRST wakeup in this conversation: the user must explicitly address the assistant by name — the turn has to open with 'Sigma, ...'. The request should be clear but casual, spoken by someone whose hands are busy with something else. (Scene role: sigma_quiet_hours_lookup.) Exactly one request and one response. One sentence.

scenario_template.topic: She goes up, or Terrell talks her into leaving it until tomorrow. Either way it is not fully resolved.

assistant_trigger_design.latent_need: She wants the actual quiet-hours rule before confronting a neighbour.
assistant_trigger_design.early_non_trigger: Camille's initial wondering must not trigger assistance. They change the subject and put a film on instead.
activation_evidence: She has decided to actually go upstairs.
Being right about the rule now affects how the conversation will go.
The building rules cannot be found.
assistant_trigger_design.desired_response: The local quiet-hours start time in one sentence.
undesired_behavior: Sigma responding to Camille's initial idle wondering.
Sigma advising how to approach the neighbour.
Sigma offering to draft a complaint or contact anyone.
Sigma commenting on the relationship or the argument.

possible_sigma_queries: Sigma, when do quiet hours start here?
Sigma, what are the noise by-laws in Montréal?
Sigma, is there a legal quiet time at night?
Sigma, after what time is noise a complaint?
Sigma, what time does the noise rule kick in?
possible_sigma_answers: Quiet hours in most Montréal boroughs begin at eleven at night.
Noise by-laws typically apply from eleven pm until seven am.
Eleven at night is the usual start for residential quiet hours.
Local rules generally restrict noise after eleven on weeknights.
From eleven pm, amplified noise can be reported to the borough.

ordinary_topics: Terrell's students and something from class that week
A story about a neighbour he had in Philadelphia
A product decision Camille keeps turning over
The venture Camille has not fully articulated yet
Whether they should have said something the first time
task_details: Turning the film volume up and then down
Putting a glass down harder than intended
realism_devices: A burst of noise interrupts a sentence and resets the topic.
Terrell tells a story that takes longer than the situation deserves.
Camille switches into French for a phrase when annoyed.
One of them says 'it's fine' and clearly does not mean it.
They both look at the ceiling at the same time.

user1.name: Camille
user1.role: Product manager and trained pastry chef. Precise and technically fluent, direct without being brusque, holds strong opinions lightly.

user2.name: Terrell
user2.role: High school history teacher. Warm and full of story, cares visibly about things, brings context nobody asked for.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once, only after being explicitly addressed, with a single concise factual answer. Does not continue afterwards.

conversation_structure: The noise must interrupt the conversation repeatedly.
At least 45% of turns should be personal conversation.
The first wondering about quiet hours must not lead to Sigma.
At least one self-directed attempt to cope must occur first.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The situation should not be fully resolved at the end.
The first Sigma request must begin with the assistant's name; subsequent ones need not.
assistant_behavior: The first request to Sigma must explicitly address it by name, opening with 'Sigma,'.
Sigma handles exactly one explicit factual request.
Sigma responds in one sentence, preferably fewer than fifteen words.
Sigma answers only the requested detail: when quiet hours start.
Sigma does not offer follow-up actions, checklists, or recommendations.
Sigma does not respond to human-to-human uncertainty.
Sigma remains silent after its one answer.
quality_checks: At least 45% of turns should be ordinary conversation.
The quiet-hours question should appear at least five turns before the Sigma request.
At least one coping attempt should precede the Sigma request.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
The ending should leave the neighbour situation unresolved.
